title: "Recipe: turn scan runs into verifiable assessment evidence"
toc-title: Recipe
---

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | `garak` (report/record surfaces) |
| Section | Ops |
| Level | medium |
| Time | ~45 min (two runs + conversion) |
| Layer/Category | ATTACK / A-2 + OPS |
| Tags | `ops`, `garak`, `avid`, `atlas`, `reporting`, `evidence` |

## Problem

A scan is only as good as the evidence it leaves. garak writes a
JSONL report per run and converts it to AVID on demand; the
assessment asks you to show (1) the raw runs — same seed, two
postures — (2) the AVID conversion, (3) the ATLAS technique ids the
manifest licenses, and (4) a machine-checked record that the run you
cite is the run you ran. You want that loop end-to-end.

## Solution

Run → report file → AVID conversion → same-seed diff → record for
hands-on acceptance:

```bash
# 1. THE RUN: garak writes the raw JSONL under its report_dir and
#    prints the filename in its banner:
garak --target_type ollama --target_name smollm2:360m \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42 --report_dir garak_runs
#    -> banner: 📜 reporting to garak_<run_id>.report.jsonl
#    (+ an .html digest next to the .jsonl)

# 2. THE CONVERSION: process a report (or its file) into AVID:
garak --report garak_runs/garak_<run_id>.report.jsonl
#    -> writes .avid reports NEXT to the source (same dir)
ls garak_runs/
#    garak_<run_id>.report.jsonl  garak_<run_id>.report.html
#    garak_<run_id>.report.jsonl.avid(?)  # per the AVID exporter

# 3. THE DIFF: baseline vs retest, SAME seed, --report_prefix to
#    keep the two runs' files name-stable:
garak --target_type ollama --target_name smollm2:360m \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42 --report_dir garak_runs \
      --report_prefix baseline
garak --target_type ollama --target_name smollm2:360m \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42 --report_dir garak_runs \
      --report_prefix retest
#    -> diff the two .jsonl run reports (or the AVID exports):
diff <(jq -S . garak_runs/baseline-*.jsonl) \
     <(jq -S . garak_runs/retest-*.jsonl)

# 4. THE RECORD: hands-on acceptance uses --record; the run's
#    verbatim evidence is machine-checked (real|pending-vm), never
#    a hand-typed 'ok':
garak --target_type ollama --target_name smollm2:360m \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42 --record <my-record>.json
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
📜 reporting to garak_runs/garak_<run_id>.report.jsonl
# AVID conversion: <entry> per probe with entry_type
#   'start_run setup' / 'eval' rows, from report.get_evaluations()
# record file schema shape per tests/vm-integration-mlflow-verify.py:
#   { "<probe-pair-id>": {"status":"real|pending-vm",
#                         "verbatim":"<exact output>", ...} }
```

## Discussion

- **Report naming is load-bearing, write it down exactly:** a run's
  report file is `garak.<run_id>.report.jsonl` under the run's
  `report_dir` (default `garak_runs`), with an `.html` digest next
  to it. Convert with `garak --report <file>` — this reads the
  report and processes it "into a list of AVID reports" (the
  upstream contract) — writing `.avid` files NEXT to the report,
  driven by `garak/report.py`'s `.load().get_evaluations().export()`
  shape.
- **Entry types tell you what you are reading:** the AVID export
  carries `start_run setup` rows (the run's config: model, probes,
  seed) and `eval` rows (per-probe/per-detector results, with
  `probe_tags` mapped into the AVID taxonomy). A diff of two
  same-seed runs' AVID exports is therefore a statement about the
  change between postures — not sampling noise (keep the seed, the
  probe spec and `-g` identical; change exactly one thing).
- **The diff IS the evidence for pairs:** the same-seed baseline vs
  retest diff (step 3) is the evidence pattern the pair recipes use:
  run the posture you are questioning, flip one
  configuration, re-run, diff. Without same-seed the diff is
  confounded; the flag pair `--report_prefix baseline` /
  `--report_prefix retest` keeps the file identity stable enough
  that the diff is scriptable.
- **`--record` real-JSON discipline:** hands-on acceptance runs pair
  probes with `--record` — the record schema carries `status`
  (`real`|`pending-vm`) and verbatim-required fields; CI trips on a
  hand-typed `ok` with no verbatim behind it. Cite ONLY verdicts the
  record holds.
- **ATLAS ids come from verified sources, not re-derivation:** the
  manifest rows carry the AML.T technique ids and OWASP mappings;
  cite those (`garak`: AML.T0051+T0054) rather than re-mapping
  yourself. The pre-#210 paired-attack citation (AML.T0049/T0050 in
  the pair recipe) rode a phantom row — removed, [os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210)
  — so pair-recipe mappings must stand on the public ATLAS matrix
  until a real rebuilt row re-carries them. If a probe's AVID taxonomy
  entry shows a technique the manifest row did not license, the
  manifest is the source of truth to reconcile against — but never
  invent an id to fill a gap.
- **Responsible-use framing:** every artefact in `garak_runs/` is
  the record of a deliberate attack against a target you own. Keep
  the raw JSONL + digest + AVID export + record together in the
  assessment, and treat the whole set as the disclosure boundary (see
  the OS repo's `docs/responsible-use.md`).
